newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates down after rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates down after rate cut.

text.p: * Central Bank lowers rates by 1.50 percentage pts
Philippine interbank call loan rates fell on Monday after the Central Bank cut its overnight rates, traders said.
The average call loan rate slid to 11.09375 percent from 12.53125. Done rates ranged from 12.00 to 11.03125 percent. Volume swelled to 25.676 billion pesos from 11.597 billion.
Out of the 61 participating financial institutions, 31 were lenders.
Earlier, the Central Bank dropped its overnight borrowing rate to 11.00 percent from 12.50 percent and its lending rate to 13.00 from 14.50.
"The Central Bank cut its overnight rates after the foreign exchange market stabilised," said a trader at a large commercial bank.
But the trader noted the Central Bank left its term rates on the reverse repos unchanged because it wanted to see first the market reaction on the peso-dollar rate.
The Central Bank raised overnight rates on two successive days last week to curb speculation on the peso.
With the drop in overnight rates, a trader said she expects Treasury bill rates to move sideways in the primary auction later.
In the secondary market, demand was for six-month bills quoted at 11.90 percent, one trader said.
There was no appetite for the one-year bills after its rate dropped sharply, while three-month bills are expected to be bought later in the auction, the same trader said.
